subject.title: [Feature]: Support custom HTTP headers on CLI WebSocket connections

question: Should Gateway CLI custom WebSocket headers become a supported core CLI/env/config surface, and if so which secret-safe sources and precedence are allowed?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but accepting arbitrary WebSocket headers changes a credential-bearing Gateway auth path and adds public CLI/env/config contract surface that automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve secret-safe core surface
options.body: Add one Gateway header contract with explicit CLI/env/config precedence, SecretInput/env substitution support, redaction, docs, and tests for CLI commands and remote config.

options.title: Limit to explicit CLI flags
options.body: Support only repeatable command-line headers for ad hoc operator use and defer persistent env/config storage until a stronger secret-handling contract is designed.

options.title: Defer to tunnels and proxy docs
options.body: Keep core unchanged and document SSH, Tailscale, cloudflared, or trusted-proxy alternatives as the supported way to reach authenticated reverse-proxy Gateways.

recommendation.title: Approve secret-safe core surface
recommendation.body: Add one Gateway header contract with explicit CLI/env/config precedence, SecretInput/env substitution support, redaction, docs, and tests for CLI commands and remote config.

likelyOwner.reason: The current Gateway CLI/call and reusable client package boundaries are most directly tied to Peter Steinberger’s recent and foundational work.
